previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, chronic malnutrition, and recurrent infections, was admitted after his visiting nurse found him hypoxic with a fever. He reported gagging while eating the night before. Imaging and labs confirmed multifocal pneumonia and a urinary tract infection, both due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He was treated with intravenous meropenem after initial broad-spectrum coverage. A video swallow study showed no aspiration, allowing resumption of soft solids and thin liquids. His sirolimus dose was reduced from 2 mg to 1 mg daily due to elevated levels. Anemia required one unit of packed red blood cells, and acute kidney injury resolved with IV fluids. He improved clinically, was weaned off supplemental oxygen, and was discharged home on a 14-day course of IV meropenem with home health services and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M w/ PMH of orthotopic liver transplant in ___ for 
alcoholic cirrhosis with indwelling foley for urinary retention 
and hx of recurrent UTIs presents with asymptomatic UTI.

Urinary tract infection- patient had urinalysis and culture 
performed at ___ on ___ and was found to have a UTI with two 
species Klebsiella and Pseudomonas.  Given that his Pseudomonas 
was almost panresistant and the Klebsiella was resistant to 
multiple antibiotics, and the patient is allergic to 
cephalosporins, quinolones, bactrim Infectious Disease was 
consulted.  They felt that because he was asymptomatic (no 
fevers, dysuria, abdominal pain etc) that this was most likely 
colonization.  In addition, when his foley was replaced on 
admission at ___ the urine culture had not grown anything at 
the time of discharge.  He is at risk for recurrent UTIs with 
his indwelling catheter. This has been addressed by urology in 
the past who recommended intermittent catheterization which has 
not happened yet. We recommended that the patient keep his 
follow-up appointment with urology to discuss this given that he 
has such high resistance patterns of his colonizers.  

** Of note. We call ___ to have the urine 
sample isolate sent to our ___ lab for further antibiotic 
sensitivties testing, however because it had been drawn on ___ 
they no longer had the isolate (they only keep them x 3days).**

S/P Orthotopic Liver transplant- patient was stable.  His ___ 
levels were elevated however his dose was also given in the 
evening prior to the level check and not 24 hours previously 
which may have falsely elevated this.  He was maintained on his 
home regimen and this will need to be rechecked as an outpatient 
and adjusted accordingly.

Pain control- patient has chronic pain. He was continued on his 
home regimen of pain meds while here and did not require any 
breakthrough medications.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

It was a pleasure caring for you while you were admitted to 
___.
You were admitted to the hospital for concern about a urinary 
tract infection.  We found this through tests on the urine 
sample that you had at ___ last week.  
Because you have many allergies to antibiotics and the bacteria 
are resistant to multiple drugs we admitted you for concern that 
we would need to start you on IV antibiotics.  However, here you 
were seen by the infectious disease specialists who felt that 
because you were not sick with the infection that we do not need 
to treat you at this time.
If you develop any burning with urination, fevers, chills, body 
aches you should call your PCP or the ___ ___ 
right away as these can be signs of an urine infection that will 
need to be treated.
The other question that arose was whether or not you should have 
the urinary catheter always in place because having this there 
can lead to urine infections.  You have seen urology in the past 
who felt that you might be able to have intermittent (off and 
on) catheters placed. We recommend that you follow-up with the 
urologists about this option as an outpatient.
